newsitem.title: USA: AT&T sees Q2 below Q1, but yr target intact.
newsitem.headline: AT&T sees Q2 below Q1, but yr target intact.

text.p: AT&T Corp on Monday said it expected second quarter 1997 earnings to be slightly lower than its first quarter, adjusted for one-off items, but to remain on track for the 1997 target of $3.45-$3.75 per share.

"Earnings per share should be slightly below the first quarter excluding the effects of the Skynet sale and the restructure reserve reversal," vice president and controller Maureen Tart told a conference call.
"We remain committed to the earnings target (for 1997) we gave at the analysts' meeting," she added.
AT&T reported $0.69 operating earnings per share in the quarter compared with $0.92 a year ago.
The sale during the first quarter of Skynet Satellite Services was responsible for the bulk of $600 million collected from divestments, AT&T said.
The restructuring reversal was $100 million of pre-1995 reserves not needed and written back during the quarter.
Tart said that the expectation for the cost of new initiatives for the year would be toward the upper end of the range of $0.75 to $1.00 per share given to analysts in March.

AT&T executives said that the effect of increased revenue from local services, medium-distance calling and expanded business contracts would be to sustain a bigger that usual gap between the rate of call volume growth and revenues growth.
"You are going to see a larger than normal gap, this year and in coming years," Jeffrey Weitzen, executive vice president for AT&T business markets told a conference call.

However, adjusting for changing business mix -- mainly the fact that local and medium-distance minutes are cheaper than long distance -- the normalized gap should narrow later in the year, Weitzen said.

Gail McGovern, AT&T's executive vice president for consumer markets said that while competition remained intense, the company was making some progress against the small aggressive resellers who were a problem last year.
"We are starting to hold our own..." she said.
In wireless services AT&T expects to benefit from the opening of new markets and is encouraging customers to move from analog to digital services to lessen the chance they will be poached by rivals.

McGovern said that she was now very confident about the strategy first articulated in detail at the analysts' conference in March to retain existing customers instead of spend heavily to get new ones.
She said the company was ahead of its own target in reducing the use of checks to attract customers in favor of free network minutes.

The use of databases has helped eliminate from sales pushes those customers called "spinners" who are known to switch carriers frequently to pick up promotional benefits, she said. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
